Version 0 shuffler PCB · Qspice baseline

Shuffler Build Book

Eight bricks, one model. Each stage adds a physical part of the board to the Qspice schematic and tells you what the simulation should show before you move on. Every stage is also a runnable file in stages/, so you can open any of them in Qspice and compare.

What you are building

The board sits across a three-module string. Converter 1 spans modules 1 and 2 and pushes current into the PV1/PV2 junction (KiCad net PV2+); converter 2 spans modules 2 and 3 and feeds the PV2/PV3 junction (PV3+). Each converter is two half-bridges 180° apart sharing an inverse-coupled inductor, so at 50 % duty it behaves as a low-impedance voltage equaliser between its two modules.

How the model names things

Node names are the same in the schematic and the netlist, so V(SWA1) means the same thing everywhere. The string bottom is the SPICE ground (label GND).

The single-sheet file

Everything the stages build up to is also one Qspice sheet: Version 0/Qspice/Shuffler_PCB_Baseline.qsch, with shuffler_models.lib next to it. It is electrically identical to stage 7 (same 177 netlist elements, same 57 measurements) but laid out by block, the way a hand-drawn schematic reads: title block, reference string, PV string, board capacitors and irradiance sources on the left; converter 1 and converter 2 on the right; PARAMETERS, SIMULATION and MEASUREMENTS along the bottom. Every parasitic and every setting is a .param in the PARAMETERS block, so the symbols on the sheet carry names such as {Ld_pkg} or {Rsn} and the sheet is edited in one place.

Editing it

to changewhere
switching period, dead time, logic level, 12 V rail, gate and bootstrap resistorsPARAMETERS, first group: Tsw, Tdead, Vlogic, Vreg, Ron, Roff, Rboot
bench load and irradiance patternRmpp, Icc, CASE, LOADSEL; the two .step lines in SIMULATION sweep CASE 1–3 and LOADSEL 0–1, delete them to run a single case
module capacitance, cable, capacitor ESR / ESL, package leads, sensor conductorCpv, Rcab, Lcab, ESR130, ESL130, Ld_pkg, Ls_pkg, Rtmcs, Ltmcs
snubber and HF-capacitor footprintsCsn, Rsn, Chf (1 pF = not fitted); sweep them with .step param Csn list … as the SIMULATION notes show
board copperR_T1 … L_gBB2, one R / L pair per KiCad net; or rerun pcb_parasitics.py and regenerate
MOSFET modelthe .model STD45N10F7 line in shuffler_models.lib: paste the FET-modeller line in its place, the symbols keep working
driver, PV module, inductor, sensor, trace modelsthe .subckt blocks in the same library (pvmi, ERUC23-4R1K, ED3140, TMCS1126, trace)

Hand edits and the generator do not mix: python gen_shuffler.py --report --verify rewrites the sheet from gen_shuffler.py and parasitics.json. Either edit the sheet and keep it under a new name, or change the generator and regenerate. --verify netlists the schematic with QUX, compares it with the generated netlist and has QSPICE64 parse it, so a broken edit of the generator is caught before a run. After a run the measurements are in QPOST's output, or in results/REPORT.meas.json from python run_baseline.py REPORT.

1

PV string and the two bench loads

Three Aiko modules in series with one lumped bypass diode each, a current sense source per module, the behavioural bench load, and an identical reference string that never gets a converter. Everything later is compared with that reference.

26 netlist elements · stages/S1.qsch
refpartQspice value / attributes
Xpv1..3PV module, Karmalkar–Haneefa explicit modelpvmi_aiko (E pin = irradiance in W/m²)
BE1..3irradiance sourcesV=table(CASE, 1,1000, 2,1000, 3,1000) …
Dbp1..3bypass diode (one per module)dbypass
Vi1..30 V current sense, + on the module side0
Bloadbench loadI=if(LOADSEL<0.5, V(PV1P)/Rmpp, Icc)
Xpvr1..3, Brefreference string (no converters)same as above, nets R1P R2P R3P
added in this stagealready placed

Place it in Qspice

  1. Add .lib shuffler_models.lib as a directive; the library holds every model used in this book.
  2. Place three pvmi_aiko boxes in series between labels PV1P, PV2P, PV3P and ground GND. Each E pin gets its own label E1…E3.
  3. Drive E1–E3 from behavioural sources with V=table(CASE, …) so one .step param CASE list 1 2 3 sweeps the irradiance patterns.
  4. Put a 0 V source in series with every module anode, + towards the module: I(Vi1) is then the module current.
  5. Load: one behavioural current source I=if(LOADSEL<0.5, V(PV1P)/Rmpp, Icc) with .param Rmpp=8.148 Icc=10 and .step param LOADSEL list 0 1.
  6. Copy the string to nets R1P R2P R3P with its own load Bref: the unshuffled reference.
  7. .tran 0 2m 1.9m 1u, .option savepowers, and the .meas lines listed in stages/S1.cir.

What you should see

At 1000 W/m² and the 8.15 Ω load the string sits on the maximum power point: about 115 V, 14.2 A, 1633 W (three times 38.4 V × 14.2 A). Shade the middle module to 600 W/m² and the plain string bypasses it: its voltage goes to −0.4 V (the diode) and the string drops to about 900 W. With the 10 A sink the same thing happens at 10 A. Shuffled and reference strings are identical here, which is the point.

Capacitors that are actually on the board

The four 130 µF hybrid-polymer capacitors (C1 across module 1, C2 and C3 across module 2, C4 across module 3) and a 10 nF terminal capacitance per PV module. Nothing else: the RC snubber and HF-cap footprints are placeholders until stage 8.

33 netlist elements · stages/S2.qsch
refpartQspice value / attributes
C1..C4TDK B40910A0137M000, 130 µF hybrid polymer130u RSER=28m
Cpv1..3module terminal capacitance (ballpark)10n RSER=0.1
added in this stagealready placed

Place it in Qspice

  1. C1 between PV1P and PV2P; C2 and C3 both between PV2P and PV3P; C4 between PV3P and GND. Give each the RSER=28m attribute (second text line of the symbol).
  2. Cpv across each module's own terminals.

What you should see

The same DC numbers as S1. The capacitors only add a settling time of a few hundred microseconds, which is why every later stage waits 2.4 ms before measuring.

3

Converter 1 power stage, ideal gate pulses

Two half-bridges of STD45N10F7 between PV1P and PV3P, the ERUC23-4R1K coupled inductor from the two switch nodes, the TMCS1126 conductor paths, and the common node into PV2P. Gates are driven by ideal 12 V pulses through 4.7 Ω so that only the power stage is on trial.

50 netlist elements · stages/S3.qsch
refpartQspice value / attributes
MTA1 MBA1 MTB1 MBB1STD45N10F7 (Q1–Q4 in KiCad)STD45N10F7 (VDMOS estimate in the lib)
XL1TDK ERUC23-4R1K coupled inductorERUC23-4R1K — pins 1,2 = sensor side, 3,4 = switch nodes
XsA1 XsB1TMCS1126B4 conductor pathTMCS1126 RSH=0.7m LSH=0.5n
VsA1 VsB10 V sense, + on the inductor side0

added in this stagealready placed

Place it in Qspice

  1. Leg A: NMOS MTA1 drain on PV1P, source on SWA1; MBA1 drain on SWA1, source on PV3P. Leg B the same with SWB1. The bulk (4th) pin of a VDMOS is tied to the source.
  2. Inductor box: pin 4 to SWA1, pin 3 to SWB1, pin 1 to LA2_1, pin 2 to LB2_1. This is the KiCad pin numbering; the model is inverse-coupled (Turns 1, −1).
  3. From LA2_1 and LB2_1 through a 0 V sense source and a TMCS1126 box into PV2P.
  4. Gate pulses: top-A high from 0 to 2.3 µs, bottom-A high from 2.5 to 4.8 µs; leg B shifted by 2.5 µs. That is 50 % minus the 200 ns dead time at each edge. Reference each pulse source to its own FET source node.
  5. .tran 0 2.5m 2.4m 20n so the last 20 cycles are saved with enough points.

What you should see

Two triangular inductor currents 180° apart with a large ripple (about 7 A pk-pk per phase at 200 kHz with this inductor). With all three modules at 1000 W/m² the average currents are zero: the converter idles and costs about 1 W. Shade module 2 to 600 W/m² and converter 1 pushes about 6 A into PV2P; with the resistor load the string makes +258 W more than the reference string, with the 10 A sink +391 W. Do not push the sink much higher in this single-converter test: one equaliser can only hold (14.9 + 8.9)/2 ≈ 11.9 A of string current with module 2 at 600 W/m², and at 12 A the model runs away (see Findings). Module 3 shading is untouched by converter 1.

Read the switch node: it swings between the converter's rails, i.e. the sum of two module voltages (about 77 V at full sun), and dips to −0.9 V during the dead time while the body diode carries the current. V1 and V2 differ by a few volts at 6 A: that is the dead-time droop of an open-loop 50 % bridge, not a fault.

What you should see

Now both midpoints are held. With module 2 shaded the string makes +422 W (resistor) / +398 W (10 A sink) relative to the reference; with module 3 at 400 W/m² it is +283 W / +340 W. With two converters the 10 A case turns positive again: the shaded module's shortfall is now shared by both neighbours instead of dragging one of them to short circuit. 5

Real gate drive: 1ED3140, 10 R / 4R7, bootstrap, 12 V rails

The ideal pulse sources are replaced by the Gate_Drivers sheet: one isolated 1ED3140 per FET with a 10 Ω source path (OUTH) and 4.7 Ω sink path (OUTL), the IN+/IN− cross-conduction interlock, a 12 V rail per converter (the Würth module, modelled as an ideal 12 V referenced to the converter's bottom rail), VSSA210 bootstrap diodes behind 10 Ω, and 100 nF ∥ 10 µF bootstrap capacitors. PWM comes from 3.3 V logic sources.

added in this stagealready placed

Place it in Qspice

  1. Each driver box: IN+ on its own PWM net, IN− on the complementary PWM of the same leg (top driver: IN+ = A_H, IN− = A_L; bottom driver the other way round). That reproduces the wiring on the sheet and the hardware interlock.
  2. Top drivers: VCC2 on BOOTA1/BOOTB1, VEE2 on the switch node. Bottom drivers: VCC2 on VREG1, VEE2 on the converter's bottom rail.
  3. OUTH → 10 Ω → gate, OUTL → 4.7 Ω → gate. Turn-on is the slow edge, turn-off the fast one.
  4. Bootstrap: VREG1 → 10 Ω → VSSA210 → BOOTA1; 100 nF and 10 µF from BOOTA1 to SWA1.

What you should see

Gate-source pulses of 12 V with a visible 200 ns gap between the bottom FET turning off and the top FET turning on (the tdead1 measurement), the bootstrap voltage sagging by a fraction of a volt each cycle and recovering while the bottom FET is on, and the same power numbers as stage 4 within a few watts.

6

Copper, package, ESL and cable parasitics

Lumped R + L in the rails, switch nodes, sensor paths and gate loops (from the board file), TO-252 lead inductances, 15 nH behind each 130 µF, and 1.5 m of 4 mm² cable per module lead. All numbers live in parasitics.json; regenerate it with python pcb_parasitics.py or edit it by hand. Every inductance carries a parallel damping resistance (5 Ω on the board, 50 Ω on the cables): without it the nanohenry loops ring against the MOSFET capacitances with a Q above 100 and the solver stalls. From this stage on the snubber and HF-capacitor footprints are also in the netlist at 1 pF, i.e. present but not fitted.

What the sweep says

With the copper and package numbers from stage 6 the switch node overshoots by only a volt or two, so the snubbers are not needed for voltage stress; what they do is soften the −3 to −4 V dip during the dead time. The resistor dissipation is well below the textbook C·V²·f because the 7 A inductor ripple swings the node during the dead time (near zero-voltage switching), so a few hundred pF costs tens of milliwatts. That trick stops working for large capacitors: the dead time can only move about 7 A × 200 ns = 1.4 µC, i.e. 14 V on 100 nF, so the 100 nF parts currently on the BOM would be hard-switched at up to C·V²·f ≈ 100 W each. Every position here sees the full two-module voltage, so rate the parts for that.

Findings while building the model

check before testingConverter 2 schematic: Q6 source not wired to the bottom rail.

In Shuffle_Converter.kicad_sch the local net M_B_Aph_S (Q6 source, C82–C84, driver VEE2) is not joined to Input_B; converter 1's sheet is wired correctly and the PCB has Q6 pad 3 on GND. The board is fine, but the schematic and board are out of sync. Updating the PCB from the schematic would disconnect that source.

voltage marginEach FET blocks the sum of two module voltages, plus the ringing.

The switch node swings between the converter's rails (stage 3 plot): about 77 V at MPP with the Aiko parameters, 87 V with the 10 A sink (modules near 43 V each), and up to 93 V at open circuit. With the copper and package parasitics of stage 6 the edges overshoot by 10–14 V, so the simulated peak drain voltage reaches 100 V in the sink case — the rating of the STD45N10F7. A lower-Voc test module gives margin; the snubber sweep in stage 8 shows how much the overshoot can be trimmed.

physicsOpen-loop 50 % is an equaliser, not an optimiser.

With the resistor load it recovers most of the shaded module's power. With a stiff current sink it pulls both modules of a pair toward their short-circuit currents; compare the stage 3 and 4 tables before reading a bench result as good or bad.

bench limitDo not run the current-sink test above about 11 A with one converter.

One equalising converter can hold at most (Iscfull + Iscshaded)/2 ≈ 11.9 A of string current when the middle module is at 600 W/m². At 12 A the model has no steady state: module 1 collapses into its bypass diode and the inductor current ramps without limit (150 A within 50 µs in the simulation). On the bench that is the electronic load hitting its compliance limit or the converter fuse. The baseline therefore uses a 10 A sink.

physicsDead time causes a few volts of V1–V2 droop at 6 A.

With 200 ns of body-diode conduction per edge at 5 µs period the effective output resistance of the bridge is set by the ripple polarity at each edge; that is what keeps the two modules a few volts apart.

ratingC91–C96 sit across Input_T–Input_B.

The rail-to-rail HF positions see the two-module voltage (77–93 V), not one module; the 50 V KGM21NR71H104KM part in the BOM is under-rated there (already noted for rectification).

approximationMOSFET, driver and copper models are ballpark by design.

STD45N10F7 is a VDMOS estimated from datasheet headline numbers; swap in the Qspice MOSFET-generator model when ready. The 1ED3140 is behavioural (70 ns, 1.4 Ω / 1.0 Ω, UVLO 8 V). Copper lumps come from pour bounding boxes with a 0.5 proximity factor on inductance.

model noteThe PV model is clamped at zero volts.

The Karmalkar–Haneefa power law (V/Voc)^m is undefined for a reverse-biased (bypassed) module, and the original expression made the simulator crawl at picosecond steps whenever a bypass diode was conducting. The library keeps the original as pvmi_orig and uses max(V,0) in pvmi; above 0 V the two are identical. The reference string also carries the 10 nF module capacitance for the same reason.

Run it

cd "Version 0/Qspice/PCB_Baseline"
python pcb_parasitics.py          # optional: refresh parasitics.json from the board file
python gen_shuffler.py --verify   # regenerate stages/S*.qsch + S*.cir, check each schematic with QUX and QSPICE64
python gen_shuffler.py --report --verify   # regenerate ../Shuffler_PCB_Baseline.qsch (the single-sheet file)
python run_baseline.py            # QSPICE64 + QPOST on every stage -> results/   (add REPORT to include the single sheet)
python build_book.py              # rebuild this page with the new numbers

The single report-grade file is Version 0/Qspice/Shuffler_PCB_Baseline.qsch (with shuffler_models.lib next to it): the complete model of stage 7 on one sheet, laid out by block, with every parasitic and setting as a .param in its PARAMETERS block. stages/S7.qsch is the same circuit in the stage layout. The .step directives sweep irradiance and load, so one run produces all six columns of the baseline table.
